text:
For running, I'd pick one of these open-ear earbuds. I could only read SoundGuys' roundup. WIRED and Runner's World wouldn't load, so I haven't checked their picks, and I didn't test anything myself.

**My picks**

- **Best budget: Soundcore AeroFit 2.** It has four-position adjustable ear hooks, IP55 sweat and water resistance, multipoint and wireless charging. SoundGuys lists it at about $79.99 on Amazon. Owners say the touch controls are oversensitive and real battery life is closer to 6 hours than the claimed 10.
  - A Dealectric page says code AFSC20 takes $25.99 off at Soundcore's US store, which would make it $104 from $129.99. I couldn't verify that, and the price differs from SoundGuys', so check the cart before you buy.
  - [Dealectric buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- **Best overall: Nothing Ear (Open).** It has strong bass for an open design, IP54 resistance, an EQ in the app and multipoint. SoundGuys lists it at about $99 on Amazon, down from $149. It's a clip-style design, so try the fit before a long run.
- **Most sweat-proof: HUAWEI FreeClip 2.** It's IP57, lightweight, and either earbud fits either ear. It costs about $200, and the fit takes some care.
- **Most secure fit and best features: Sony LinkBuds Open.** It has a stabilizer fin and 9.5 hours of battery. It's rated IPX4, which is less sweat protection than the others. SoundGuys lists it around $158, down from $230.
- **Runner-up for battery and buttons: Shokz OpenFit 2.** It has 11 hours of battery and physical buttons that work with gloves. It costs about $180.

**Other options**
- **Bone conduction.** The Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 was in your search, but I couldn't read its review. SoundGuys says bone conduction generally sounds worse than open-ear earbuds, but it sits very securely.
- **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds.** They cost about $299, which is steep for running.
- **AirPods 4.** They're a good fit for iPhone users but come in one size with no swappable tips.

**How to choose:** Fit matters most for running. If you're unsure, start with the AeroFit 2, since its adjustable hooks suit different ear sizes. If you run in heavy rain or sweat a lot, the FreeClip 2 is the safest bet.

Source: [SoundGuys: Best open-ear headphones and earbuds](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

| Pick | Category | Price (listed) | Pros | Cons / Caveats |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** | Best overall | $99 at Amazon (MSRP $149) | Strong bass for an open design, IP54, parametric EQ in the app, multipoint, customizable pinch controls | The article doesn't list cons. Its body text cites $149.99, which conflicts with the $149 MSRP |

One owner found the sound too bright and needed EQ. Another said it lacks the benefits of AirPods 3 Pro |
| **Sony LinkBuds Open** | Best features | $157.95 at Amazon (MSRP $229.99) | 9.5-hour battery, flexible stabilizer fin, wide-area tap controls, Auto Switch and multipoint | Typical open-earbud sound tradeoffs. The article's body text lists $199.99, which differs from the listed MSRP |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** | Best budget | $79.99 at Amazon (MSRP $99.99) | Four-position adjustable ear hooks, IP55, multipoint, 23 EQ presets, wireless charging | Touch controls are very sensitive. One owner reports about 6 h real-world battery vs. 10 h claimed. The AeroFit Pro ($179.99, IPX5) is a separate model |
| **HUAWEI FreeClip 2** | Best clip-on | $199.99 at Amazon | Lightweight, either earbud works in either ear, IP57, good battery, decent bass when fitted well | Expensive. Fit matters, and they block no outside noise (which is the point) |

**Notable mentions**
- **Shokz OpenFit 2** ($179.95): 11-hour battery, physical buttons that work with gloves.
- **Shokz OpenFit 2+** ($199.95): AI-filtered call quality, wireless charging, less sound leakage.
- **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** ($299): clip-on option, but expensive.

**Running-relevant notes**
- **Sweat/weather protection:** HUAWEI FreeClip 2 (IP57) is the most rated. Nothing Ear (Open) and AirPods 4 are IP54, and Soundcore AeroFit 2 is IP55. Sony LinkBuds Open is IPX4-equivalent.
- **Secure fit while moving:** AeroFit 2's adjustable hooks suit varied ear sizes. Sony's stabilizer fin is designed for a secure, comfortable fit. The article says fit is the top priority for open-ear models.
- **Awareness:** All open designs let ambient sound through, which suits road and trail runners.
- **Budget:** AeroFit 2 is the lowest-cost option, though its battery and touch controls drew owner complaints.
- **Alternative:** Bone conduction headphones leave the ear canal open and are an option if you want a different approach to awareness, though the article notes their sound quality is generally lower.
